benefits: Adds a dreamy neon halo around any photo or logo — the gaming-thumbnail look in one click.
Works beautifully on dark backgrounds where the glow has room to bloom.
The tinted-blur technique keeps the original sharp underneath — detail is never sacrificed.
Live sliders mean you see the exact result before downloading; no guesswork.

faqs.a: The image is blurred, tinted with your glow color, and composited behind the sharp original using a screen blend. The blur spreads light outward (the halo), the tint colors it, and the original on top keeps everything crisp.

Radius controls how far the halo spreads (0 = tight edge light, 60 = wide dreamy bloom). Intensity controls how bright the halo is. Combine a wide radius with medium intensity for the classic neon look.
faqs.q: What is the difference between radius and intensity?

faqs.a: Any color — the glow layer is tinted with your exact pick. Neon cyan (#00E5FF), magenta (#FF2FB3), and warm amber (#FFB020) are popular; indigo (#4F46E5) matches this site's theme.
Transparent logos and PNGs with alpha glow around their actual shape, because the blur respects transparency. The effect is especially clean on stickers and emblems.
faqs.q: Does it work on transparent PNGs?

faqs.a: The preview is capped at 1400 px on the long edge; the PNG download matches the preview. The blur radius scales with the image, so results look the same at any size.
The glow uses canvas blur filters, supported by all modern browsers. Very old browsers may render a sharper, flatter halo instead of a soft bloom.
faqs.q: Will it work in my browser?

glow-effect.formula:
glowLayer = blur(image, radius) tinted with glowColor
screen(a, b) = 1 - (1 - a) x (1 - b) per channel
result = screen(glowLayer x2 at intensity alpha) then original drawn on top
Example: radius 24 px, intensity 60% -> tinted blur drawn twice at 0.6 alpha with screen blend.
howTo: Upload a photo or logo from your device (up to 15 MB).
Pick your glow color with the color picker.
Drag the radius slider to set how far the halo spreads.
Drag the intensity slider to set how bright the glow is.
Press Download to save the glowing image as a PNG.
keyFacts: Creates a soft neon halo by blurring a tinted copy of the image behind the sharp original.
Glow color picker with live hex readout — any color works.
Radius slider (0–60 px) controls halo spread; intensity slider (0–100%) controls brightness.
Screen-blend compositing keeps the glow luminous without washing out the image.

limitations: Rendering is capped at 1400 px on the long edge, so huge originals are scaled down first.
Very old browsers without canvas blur filters render a flatter, sharper halo.
The glow is a photographic bloom, not a true light simulation — it cannot cast light on surroundings.
Heavy glow on busy photos can look muddy; it shines brightest on dark, simple images.
